interest: Shows French colonial surveillance of Japanese firm Dainan Koosi in Saigon, raided in 1938 as a suspected espionage front.
overview: This file (894.20251G/1051) from the U.S. State Department records relates to Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, and espionage in French Indochina during October 1938. The primary document is Despatch No. 7 from American Consul Peter H. A. Flood in Saigon, reporting that French military authorities conducted a raid on October 18, 1938, against the premises of Dainan Koosi, the second-largest Japanese trading firm in Saigon after Mitsui. French authorities seized extensive corporate archives on suspicion of espionage and commenced translating them, an action closely linked to the arrest of the mixed-blood editor of the local newspaper 'L'Alerte' for allegedly aiding Japanese agents. The file preserves the complete set of despatch copies (original, duplicate, triplicate, and quadruplicate), followed by an extraneous court transcript fragment concerning witness testimony and an internal Department of State charge slip routing File 894.202 to Mr. Henry.
